subject: Chemistry
unit: Unit I — Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry
title: Eudiometry & Gas Mixture Analysis
quickSummary: Eudiometry analyzes gas combustion and selective volume absorptions. Water vapor condenses to liquid, producing a combustion contraction of ΔV₁ = 1 + y/4 volumes, while passing through KOH produces a contraction of ΔV₂ = x volumes (= V_CO₂).
summary: Master eudiometric volume contraction formulas and selective chemical absorbers.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 8. Eudiometry & Selective Chemical Absorbers
conceptBreakdown.title: 8. Eudiometry & Selective Chemical Absorbers

summaryBox.title: Selective Absorbers Reference
summaryBox.takeaway: KOH absorbs CO2/SO2; Alkaline Pyrogallol absorbs O2; Turpentine Oil absorbs O3; CaCl2 absorbs H2O; Ammoniacal Cu2Cl2 absorbs CO.

conceptBreakdown.content:
Eudiometry is the quantitative gas-phase analytical method used to determine molecular formulas of gaseous hydrocarbons and analyze gas mixture compositions through explosion and selective absorption:

• **$\text{CO}_2, \text{SO}_2$** → Concentrated $\text{KOH}$ solution
• **$\text{O}_2$** → Alkaline Pyrogallol solution
• **$\text{H}_2\text{O}$ vapor** → Anhydrous $\text{CaCl}_2$ / $\text{Mg(ClO}_4)_2$ / Conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$
• **$\text{CO}$** → Ammoniacal Cuprous Chloride ($\text{Cu}_2\text{Cl}_2$)
• **$\text{O}_3$ (Ozone)** → Turpentine Oil / Cinnamon Oil
• **$\text{NO}_2$** → Water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$)
• **$\text{NH}_3$** → Dilute Acid / Water

conceptBreakdown.heading: 8.1 General Hydrocarbon Combustion Equation in Eudiometry
conceptBreakdown.title: 8.1 General Hydrocarbon Combustion Equation in Eudiometry
conceptBreakdown.content:
For a gaseous hydrocarbon $\text{C}_x\text{H}_y$ burned in excess $\text{O}_2$ at constant T and P (where produced $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ condenses to liquid with negligible volume):

$$\text{C}_x\text{H}_y (g) + \left(x + \frac{y}{4}\right)\text{O}_2 (g) \longrightarrow x \text{ CO}_2 (g) + \frac{y}{2} \text{ H}_2\text{O} (l)$$
$$\text{1 Vol} \quad : \quad \left(x + \frac{y}{4}\right)\text{ Vol} \quad : \quad x \text{ Vol} \quad : \quad 0 \text{ Vol (liquid)}$$

• **Contraction upon Combustion ($\Delta V_1$)**:
  $$\Delta V_1 = V_{\text{reactants}} - V_{\text{products}} = \left(1 + x + \frac{y}{4}\right) - x = \mathbf{1 + \frac{y}{4} \text{ Volumes}}$$

• **Contraction upon KOH Addition ($\Delta V_2$)**:
  $$\Delta V_2 = V_{\text{CO}_2} = \mathbf{x \text{ Volumes}}$$

quickRevision: ΔV₂ (KOH contraction) = x volumes = volume of CO2.
Pyrogallol absorbs O2; Turpentine absorbs O3.
